name: Croatia
summary: Croatia's electric-car market is small but grew quickly in 2026: Eurostat counts about 7,100 battery-electric passenger cars on the road at the end of 2025, and ACEA reports 1,781 new BEVs in January–June 2026, about four and a half times the same period of 2025. Public charging is run by 32 companies, led by HEP's ELEN network, Petrol and Hrvatski Telekom, with published prices of about €0.35–0.42/kWh for AC and €0.66–0.78/kWh for fast DC without a subscription. Home wallboxes are sold by solar and electrical firms, the supplier E.ON, online shops and a DIY chain at roughly €475–1,500 for the unit; in apartment buildings, installing charging points is a co-owners' decision taken by a majority of ownership shares under the building-management law in force since 2025.

buildings.topic: Who decides in a multi-unit building
buildings.text: Decisions on installing ducting and charging points for electric vehicles, 'vodeći računa o sigurnosti u slučaju požara' (with regard to fire safety), are listed among building-management decisions. Such a decision is adopted when co-owners holding more than 50% of the co-ownership shares vote for it; a qualified majority is reserved for other listed decisions.
buildings.law: Zakon o upravljanju i održavanju zgrada (NN 152/24, 47/26), Art. 39(1), 39(3) item 10 and 39(4); in force since 01.01.2025
buildings.source_title: Zakon.hr – Zakon o upravljanju i održavanju zgrada

buildings.text: 'Na mjestima za punjenje električnih vozila u zgradama ili na zgradama potrebno je primijeniti mjere zaštite od požara' – fire-protection measures must be applied at charging points in or on buildings.
buildings.law: Zakon o upravljanju i održavanju zgrada, Art. 20(7)
buildings.source_title: Zakon.hr – Zakon o upravljanju i održavanju zgrada

buildings.text: No provision letting one co-owner install a charger in common parts without a co-owners' decision was found in the consolidated text; the law deals with charging points through the decision rule above.
buildings.law: Zakon o upravljanju i održavanju zgrada
buildings.source_title: Zakon.hr – Zakon o upravljanju i održavanju zgrada

buildings.text: Costs of the building's common parts are shared among co-owners 'razmjerno njihovim suvlasničkim dijelovima' (in proportion to their co-ownership shares).
buildings.law: Zakon o upravljanju i održavanju zgrada, Art. 28
buildings.source_title: Zakon.hr – Zakon o upravljanju i održavanju zgrada

buildings.text: In a reported case at a new apartment building in Zagreb, the owner ran a 40 m three-phase cable from his apartment through conduit laid by the developer to his outdoor parking space and connected the charger to his own apartment meter; he said no paperwork was needed ('Od papira za to ne treba apsolutno ništa'). He also said fire inspectors were refusing chargers in underground garages although, in his view, no rule requires this.

buildings.text: In August 2026 a draft 'Pravilnik o građevinama i radovima za koje nije potrebna građevinska dozvola' was put to public consultation; critics fear it could require extra design documentation and a longer procedure for home wallboxes. The draft was not final.

No company advertising a subscription charging service for residential buildings was found (re-charge.hr could not be checked).

buildings.text: The recast Energy Performance of Buildings Directive (EU) 2024/1275 calls for removing barriers to recharging infrastructure 'such as split incentives and administrative complications' (recital 50). buildings.text: Croatia's law on alternative-fuels infrastructure deals with publicly accessible charging; for non-public charging points it only says the national policy framework may include measures to encourage and ease their installation.

policy.text: Under the EU Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR, (EU) 2023/1804), Croatia must provide publicly accessible charging with a total power of at least 1.3 kW per registered battery-electric car or van and 0.80 kW per plug-in hybrid (Art. 3(1)).
On the TEN-T core network, AFIR requires charging pools at most 60 km apart with at least 400 kW in total by 31.12.2025 and 600 kW by 31.12.2027, each with at least one 150 kW point (Art. 3).

AFIR requires ad hoc payment without a contract at all public charging points, and card payment at points of 50 kW or more installed from 13.04.2024; existing ones on the TEN-T network must follow by 01.01.2027 (Art. 5).

Croatia's 2017 national policy framework for alternative fuels (NN 34/2017) set minimum targets of 602 public charging sockets at 348 stations by 2025 (434 AC, 168 DC of 50 kW+) and 806 sockets at 479 stations by 2030 (554 AC, 252 DC); whether these targets have been updated was not checked.

gaps: WebSearch quota ran out midway; later checks used only WebFetch on known URLs, so some installers and 2026 sources may be missing.

Official public charger count: the EU Alternative Fuels Observatory shows Croatian figures only in interactive charts that could not be read, and the national CRO-IDRO registry was not reachable; the count used is a media figure (Lider).
Home chargers: no installer based in Rijeka with its own website listing charger work was found (trebam.hr lists local providers only as a marketplace); Njuškalo was not checked.

Sites that did not load (robots.txt timeout or DNS error): aledo-tech.hr, ses-croatia.com (Soft Energy Systems, Zadar/Zagreb), re-charge.hr, chargingshop.hr, kralj.hr, ams.hr, evshop.com.hr, energycentar.hr, cee.hr, elektricna-vozila.com.hr, elektroinstalacije-sporcic.com, shop.autohrvatska.hr, zenerg.hr, molplugee.hr, tifon.hr; cvh.hr returned error 521; Petrol's home-charger page returned 404 (Petrol only mentions 'financiranje pri kupnji e-punionice').
E.ON home-charger pages load via JavaScript; prices not visible. HGSPOT product pages returned no product data. No HEP home-charger offer was found on the HEP pages checked.

Electricity: HEP Elektra's universal-service tariff table in force since 01.11.2025 (energy prices and supply fee up to 30.09.2026) is published only as an image and was not read; the VAT rate on household electricity was not confirmed.
ELEN: BUCO (19.12.2025) reported new motorway prices of 0,50/0,60 €/kWh, but elen.hep.hr still lists the price list of 01.04.2025 as current (checked 23.09.2026); the official list is used here.
IONITY subscription per-kWh prices were read inconsistently from the dynamic page (Power 365: 0.39–0.44 €/kWh; Motion 365: 0.53–0.55 €/kWh) – check in the app.

Prices not published by the operator or not readable: Tesla (for other EVs), Kaufland, Hrvatski Telekom eSpots (no official page found), MOL Plugee, Qelo (image); Electrip, Eleport, GreenWay and MOON prices not checked.

EV fleet: CVH/MUP statistics by fuel type were not found; Eurostat's 2025 BEV stock (7,058) is below its 2024 value (7,286) as published. A media figure of 0.6% BEV share of the fleet (pvinformer.me, 18.08.2026) does not match the Eurostat dataset (about 0.34%) and is not used.
2026 registrations: ACEA releases after June 2026 were not found; January–June 2026 is the latest period used.
Subsidies: the EnU-4/26 deadline-extension decision (PDF) has no readable text; remaining budget not published.

Buildings: Croatia's transposition of the EPBD recast charging provisions, the full text of the August 2026 draft regulation on permit-free works, HEP ODS rules and fees for a separate charger connection in a building, and the Strujni krug members-only building guide were not checked.
